\begin{definition}[Nonzero binary vector equivalence]
\lean{FABL.nonzeroBinaryVectorEquiv}
\label{FABL.nonzeroBinaryVectorEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube}
For every natural number $\ell$, there is an equivalence between the finite set of size
$2^\ell-1$ and the set of nonzero vectors in the binary cube of length $\ell$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Nonzero binary columns]
\lean{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn}
\statementsource{Vad12}{

  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p146-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p170-b003
}
\label{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.nonzeroBinaryVectorEquiv}
Let $\ell$ and $n$ be nonnegative integers with $n\le 2^\ell-1$. For each
$j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define its column to be the nonzero binary vector of length
$\ell$ assigned to the index $j$ by the standard bijection between the indices
$0,\ldots,2^\ell-2$ and nonzero binary vectors of length $\ell$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonvanishing of the enumerated vectors]
\lean{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn_ne_zero}
\label{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.nonzeroBinaryVectorEquiv, FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\ell,n$ be nonnegative integers with $n\le 2^\ell-1$, and let
$j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The vector assigned to $j$ by the enumeration of nonzero vectors
in $\mathbb F_2^\ell$ is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the nonzero-vector enumeration]
\lean{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn_injective}
\label{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn_injective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.nonzeroBinaryVectorEquiv, FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\ell,n$ be nonnegative integers with $n\le 2^\ell-1$. The map that assigns to each
index $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ the corresponding enumerated nonzero vector in $\mathbb
F_2^\ell$ is injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Pairwise independent matrix]
\lean{FABL.pairwiseIndependentMatrix}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p065-b004,

  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p146-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p170-b003
}
\label{FABL.pairwiseIndependentMatrix}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn, FABL.𝔽₂}
For natural numbers $\ell$ and $n$ satisfying $n \le 2^\ell - 1$, define the $\ell\times
n$ matrix over the field with two elements whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$ is the
$i$th coordinate of the pairwise independent column associated with $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Columns of the pairwise independent matrix]
\lean{FABL.pairwiseIndependentMatrix_column}
\label{FABL.pairwiseIndependentMatrix_column}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn, FABL.pairwiseIndependentMatrix}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\ell,n$ be nonnegative integers with $n\le 2^\ell-1$, and form the matrix whose
$j$th column is the vector assigned to $j$ by the enumeration of nonzero vectors in
$\mathbb F_2^\ell$. For every $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the $j$th column, viewed as a
vector, equals that assigned vector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of selected matrix columns]
\lean{FABL.matrixColumnSum_pairwiseIndependentMatrix}
\statementsource{CW79}{pdf-1c24478649f7-p009-b001}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p154-b004
}
\label{FABL.matrixColumnSum_pairwiseIndependentMatrix}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.matrixColumnSum, FABL.matrixColumnSum_apply_eq_sum, FABL.pairwiseIndependentColumn, FABL.pairwiseIndependentMatrix}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathbb{F}_2$ be the field with two elements, and let $A$ be the matrix whose $j$th column is the $j$th vector in an enumeration of the nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. For natural numbers $n$ and $m$ with $m\leq 2^n-1$, and any set $S$ of column indices, the matrix-vector product of this matrix with the indicator vector of $S$ equals the sum, over $j\in S$, of its $j$th column.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Pairwise independent row count]
\lean{FABL.pairwiseIndependentRowCount}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p170-b003}
\label{FABL.pairwiseIndependentRowCount}
\leanok
For a nonnegative integer $n$, define the row count to be
$\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil\}$, where the ceiling-logarithm denotes the least
natural number $r$ such that $2^r\ge n+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bound from the row-count parameter]
\lean{FABL.n_le_two_pow_pairwiseIndependentRowCount_sub_one}
\label{FABL.n_le_two_pow_pairwiseIndependentRowCount_sub_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pairwiseIndependentRowCount}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, set $m=\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil\}$, where the
ceiling is the least integer $t$ such that $n+1\le 2^t$. Then $n\le 2^m-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on the number of rows]
\lean{FABL.two_pow_pairwiseIndependentRowCount_le_four_mul}
\label{FABL.two_pow_pairwiseIndependentRowCount_le_four_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pairwiseIndependentRowCount}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive integer $n$, let $r$ be the least nonnegative integer such that
$n+1\le 2^r$, and set $m=\max\{1,r\}$. Then $2^m\le 4n$.
\end{theorem}
